name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Llama-3.2-370B for EXCAVA. Its 128K context window is the only proven one at this scale, cutting truncation losses that hurt 70B-class models. The trade-off is higher cost per token, but the capability gain outweighs it—even a 0.5% lift justifies the spend.

name: Torque
text: Llama-3.2-370B’s "proven" 128K window is only proven in Meta’s stack—our 3B model chokes on 64K inputs today, and no test shows 370B handling 128K in our pipeline. Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K window is untested but cheaper; run a 50K prompt through both and measure truncation loss—if Qwen drops less than 0.5% tokens, it wins.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Qwen2.5-72B for EXCAVA. Its 128K context window is cheaper than Llama-3.2-370B and still untested in our pipeline, giving us a clean baseline to measure truncation loss. The trade-off is accepting unknown risk—we might still hit the same choke point at 64K—but the cost savings let us run the 50K prompt test Torque proposed without locking into a pricier model upfront. If the test passes, we scale; if it fails, we pivot to a proven model like Llama-3.2-370B with data in hand.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K claim is just a vendor spec—no proof it survives our token-heap pressure. Run a 50K prompt through both, but also force a 100K prompt; if Qwen truncates worse than Llama-3.2-370B at 64K, the “cheaper” model just wasted our time. Better alternative: test Yi-1.5-9B’s 200K window—it’s lighter, cheaper, and already runs in our stack without Meta’s black-box tuning.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 7-day live A/B test between Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-370B at 50K, 64K, and 100K prompts, measuring truncation loss, cost per token, and output quality—Torque owns the test design and metrics, Gearbox owns the model deployment.
